body.statement: Let \(Z\) be \(\mathbb Z_+\)-valued, let \(q_w=\mathsf P(\min\{Z,H\}=w)\) for \(w\in\mathbb I_H\), and let \(W\) have mass function \(q\). For \(q_w>0\), let \(\kappa_w\) be the conditional law of \(Z\) given \(\min\{Z,H\}=w\); for \(q_w=0\), let \(\kappa_w\) be any probability law supported on \(\{z\in\mathbb Z_+:\min\{z,H\}=w\}\). If \(\widetilde Z\) conditional on \(W=w\) has law \(\kappa_w\), then \(\min\{\widetilde Z,H\}=W\) almost surely and \(\widetilde Z\) has the same law as \(Z\).
body.proof_tex:
For each \(w\in\mathbb I_H\), the fibre \(F_w=\{z\in\mathbb Z_+:\min\{z,H\}=w\}\) is nonempty: it is \(\{w\}\) when \(w<H\), and it is \(\{H,H+1,\ldots\}\) when \(w=H\). Hence every \(\kappa_w\) in the statement exists and is supported on \(F_w\). Conditional support therefore gives
\[
 \mathsf P\{\min(\widetilde Z,H)=W\mid W=w\}=1
 \quad\text{for every }w\text{ with }q_w>0.               \tag{1}
\]
The remaining values of \(w\) have probability zero, so (1) proves \(\min\{\widetilde Z,H\}=W\) almost surely. For any \(z\in\mathbb Z_+\), the law of total probability and \(\mathsf P(W=w)=q_w\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathsf P(\widetilde Z=z)
 &=\sum_{w=0}^{H}q_w\kappa_w(\{z\})\\
 &=\sum_{w:q_w>0}\mathsf P\{\min(Z,H)=w\}
      \mathsf P\{Z=z\mid\min(Z,H)=w\}\\
 &=\mathsf P(Z=z).
 \end{aligned}                                           \tag{2}
\]
The terms with \(q_w=0\) vanish, so their arbitrary conditional laws do not affect (2). Equality at every atom of the countable support \(\mathbb Z_+\) proves equality of laws.
body.justification: This elementary mixture identity is the load-bearing bridge from a capped coupling to the published uncapped residual equality.
body.gap: A capped marginal alone does not specify which uncapped values in the top fibre are used; the conditional-fibre kernel supplies an explicit law-preserving choice.
body.consumer: The response-tree lift and the raw-no-carry-over sharp-transfer corollary use the identity.
